definitions.gloss: cheap sweets; traditional penny candy; snacks for children
definitions.explanation: Inexpensive sweets and snacks, typically costing 10-50 yen each, traditionally sold in small neighborhood shops. A nostalgic part of Japanese childhood culture.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}、よく{駄菓子|だがし}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: When I was a kid, I often bought cheap sweets.

examples.japanese: {近所|きんじょ}の{駄菓子屋|だがしや}がなくなってしまった。
examples.english: The neighborhood penny candy shop closed down.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}、{駄菓子|だがし}を{大人|おとな}{買|が}いする{人|ひと}が{増|ふ}えているらしい。
examples.english: Apparently, more and more adults are buying up cheap sweets in bulk these days.

notes:
A culturally significant term. {駄菓子屋|だがしや} (penny candy shops) were once found in every neighborhood and were an important part of children's after-school life. Though many have closed, they remain a powerful symbol of nostalgia in Japan.

The {駄|だ} prefix means "inferior" or "cheap" (as in {駄目|だめ}), contrasting with {和菓子|わがし} (refined Japanese sweets).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {駄菓子屋|だがしや} (penny candy shop)
- {駄菓子|だがし}を{大人|おとな}{買|が}いする (to buy up cheap sweets as an adult — a popular expression)
- {懐|なつ}かしの{駄菓子|だがし} (nostalgic cheap sweets)
